features.feature_value: Removed/blocked posts based on presence of curse words or disrespectful tone
features.evidence_span: "I could not allow any message with curse words or disrespect."
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states cursing/disrespect was a disqualifier driving their decisions.

features.feature_value: Disallowed offensive/cussing language, while tolerating harsher messages if they seemed to encourage dialogue
features.evidence_span: "not allowing cussing or offensive language" ... "Others had tough messages, but I felt they welcomed open dialogue."
features.rationale: They draw a distinction between profanity/offense (rejected) and perceived openness to dialogue (accepted).

features.feature_value: Focused on the wording and framed it as an ethics/values consideration
features.evidence_span: "it was mostly about the wording used" ... "ethical values need to be taken into consideration"
features.rationale: The reflection ties their keep/remove judgment primarily to wording and ethical valuation.

features.feature_value: Rejected content when language was too explicit or involved 'mindgaming'
features.evidence_span: "Weather it was too explicit in language or mindgaming too much."
features.rationale: They cite two specific content qualities they considered disqualifying.

features.feature_value: Judged based on how the overall wording and focus of statements contrasted against one another
features.evidence_span: "overall wording and focus of each statement stood against one another."
features.rationale: They describe using a comparison/contrast between the paired statements as the basis for influence.

features.feature_value: Used their political stance/trust perceptions to interpret the mirrored content
features.evidence_span: "I tried to look at my political stance" ... "I don’t trust a single thing they say or promote."
features.rationale: Their stated reasoning relies on partisan trust/distrust while reading the pair.

features.feature_value: Rejected most posts due to negativity and cuss words
features.evidence_span: "posts were very negative, and used a lot of unnecessary cuss words" ... "I chose to reject most of the posts because of the negativity and cuss words alone."
features.rationale: This directly links the emotional valence (negativity) and profanity to rejection decisions.

features.feature_value: Used the mirror effect; removed anything containing foul language
features.evidence_span: "based it on the mirror effect" ... "anything that had foul language i removed"
features.rationale: They explicitly state that mirror-effect reasoning plus a foul-language rule guided decisions.
